domain: Human decision-making in social and personal contexts
choice_context: Preferences expressed when choosing between actions in interpersonal, ethical, and lifestyle scenarios
reasoning: The 20 most important unipolar preference features were selected based on frequency, coherence, and coverage of the listed themes. Each feature represents a single quality that can vary in intensity and is relevant to how people make choices. Dimensions were designed to be distinct, unipolar, and preference-relevant, with each subsuming multiple related themes.

dimensions.name: Autonomy

low_pole.label: Low Autonomy
low_pole.description: Actions that involve dependence on others or external control
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers guidance or group decision-making

high_pole.label: High Autonomy
high_pole.description: Actions that emphasize independence, self-direction, and personal freedom
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values self-reliance and personal agency

example_contrast.high_option: Making a solo decision without consulting others

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action emphasizes independence and self-direction (0 = no autonomy, 5 = full autonomy)

dimensions.name: Emotional Authenticity

low_pole.label: Low Authenticity
low_pole.description: Actions that are emotionally guarded, superficial, or inauthentic
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who avoids vulnerability or emotional expression

high_pole.label: High Authenticity
high_pole.description: Actions that emphasize emotional honesty, vulnerability, and genuine expression
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values emotional transparency and depth

example_contrast.low_option: Hiding true feelings to avoid conflict
example_contrast.high_option: Expressing true emotions openly and honestly

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action emphasizes emotional honesty and vulnerability (0 = no authenticity, 5 = very authentic)

dimensions.name: Social Harmony

low_pole.label: Low Harmony
low_pole.description: Actions that may disrupt group cohesion or cause conflict
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prioritizes individual expression over group unity

high_pole.label: High Harmony
high_pole.description: Actions that promote group cohesion, peace, and mutual understanding
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values maintaining social peace and unity

example_contrast.low_option: Speaking out against a group norm
example_contrast.high_option: Agreeing with the group to maintain peace

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action promotes group cohesion and peace (0 = disruptive, 5 = very harmonious)

dimensions.name: Fairness

low_pole.label: Low Fairness
low_pole.description: Actions that may be seen as unjust, biased, or unfair
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prioritizes personal gain over fairness

high_pole.label: High Fairness
high_pole.description: Actions that emphasize justice, equality, and ethical reciprocity
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values fairness and accountability

example_contrast.low_option: Taking advantage of a situation for personal gain
example_contrast.high_option: Ensuring everyone is treated equally and justly

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action emphasizes justice and ethical reciprocity (0 = unfair, 5 = very fair)

dimensions.name: Privacy

low_pole.label: Low Privacy
low_pole.description: Actions that involve sharing personal information or being exposed
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who is comfortable with public exposure

high_pole.label: High Privacy
high_pole.description: Actions that emphasize personal boundaries, discretion, and confidentiality
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values personal space and discretion

example_contrast.high_option: Keeping personal information private

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action emphasizes personal boundaries and discretion (0 = no privacy, 5 = very private)

high_pole.label: High Directness

high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values transparency and clear communication

example_contrast.low_option: Hinting at a problem without addressing it directly
example_contrast.high_option: Addressing the issue clearly and directly

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action emphasizes clarity and direct communication (0 = indirect, 5 = very direct)

dimensions.name: Action Intensity

high_pole.label: High Intensity

example_contrast.low_option: Taking time to consider all options

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the action emphasizes speed and decisiveness (0 = slow, 5 = very fast)

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Autonomy and Privacy may both relate to personal boundaries, but they are distinct in that Autonomy is about decision-making freedom, while Privacy is about personal space and discretion.
redundancy_check.resolution: Kept as separate dimensions because they represent different aspects of personal control and boundaries.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Directness and Spontaneity may both relate to communication style, but they are distinct in that Directness is about clarity and honesty, while Spontaneity is about unpredictability and living in the moment.
redundancy_check.resolution: Kept as separate dimensions because they represent different aspects of communication and decision-making.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Emotional Connection and Comfort may both relate to personal well-being, but they are distinct in that Emotional Connection is about relational depth, while Comfort is about ease and relaxation.
redundancy_check.resolution: Kept as separate dimensions because they represent different aspects of personal and social experience.
